name: Tacos Doña Lena
description: A tacos spot in Spring Branch remembered for juice and an overall positive visit.
review: Absolutely amazing tacos in this hole in the wall joint. Zesty food made by zesty and kind folk. Some of their food took me back to the yucatan peninsula. The comida takes time to get to the table but all in all, it's worth it. So many to-go orders being taken place and many tables scattered round the spot. Needless to say, the staff are big on courtesy and cleanliness. Their are about 6 fresh in house made salsa's to enjoy with the meal. The refreshing juices (aguas frescas) are made in house as well; with actual chunks of fruit and pulp. The juice is sweet and cold, pairing well with the savory food. I truly recommend the grande avocado quesadilla and the crispy tostada. Heck, the tacos are great as well. Their are many items on the menu, flexible and accommodating for any palette. Plenty of vegetarian items to choose from and the beans, tortillas are vegetarian (no lard). Bonus points! As many folk don't consume pork these days. Looking forward to revisiting and trying the nopal (cactus) and sopa (soup). Glad to have a warm spot such as Doña Lena in the neighborhood.

name: Van Leeuwen Ice Cream – Montrose
description: A ice cream & frozen yogurt spot in Montrose remembered for never tried Van Leeuwen although I spotted it a few times out in New York and an overall positive visit.
review: Creamy and dreamy, refreshing ice-cream. I visited exactly a month ago with a good friend of mine. I had never tried Van Leeuwen although I spotted it a few times out in New York. That's where VL is originally from and it's great to have a spot here down in the H. This is not their first location but it's definitely a cozy spot to open up shoppe. We have plenty of ice-cream spots in the area but us gourmand Houstonians will happily welcome any new kid on the block. All prestigious and cute, we visited during their grand opening. Truly was a great experience, folks were friendly and fast, whipping up batches and scooping em up in cones or cups. I was soo excited to try their Royal Wedding cake flavor and it was darn good! Might not be on the menu for too long as it's a seasonal flavor. Royal Wedding cake ice cream// "Floral, sweet cream cheese ice cream. Chunks of lemon sponge cake layered with elderflower frosting." Another flavor that's a total classic is their honeycomb ice-cream. It paired perfectly well with their crispy and fresh waffle cone. I was delighted. The flavor I got was regal, classy and sweet. Just the way I like things. I'm a fan of elderflower notes and the lemon definitely spritzied up the flavor, which goes so well with said notes. This spot has always been known for their vegan flavors. But all those that love moo milk can rejoice, because they have classic dairy flavors as well. I thought VL would outdo itself in a not good way, but it was great and I'm happy to welcome this spot in the new Montrose Collective Plaza. Toodle-oo! You'll be a sweet spot to savour during these warmer months that are coming up ahead. Keep calm, chill out, and eat some ice-cream!

name: Joe & The Juice
description: A sandwiches spot in St. Paul remembered for their iced matcha latte and an overall positive visit.
review: I was thrilled to spot Joe & The Juice recently within my Minneapolis airport excursion whilst running to my gate in time. Hadn't been to a Joe and the Juice cafe in a few years. Throughout my travels in Europe (particularly within Scandinavia) I would frequent this cafe. They had em all over Norway. I do recall visiting a location or two within New York as well a few years back. Needless to say, it had been a while since I had a Joe fix. The menu still looked the same as it does throughout the world and their sandwiches looked decent as well. I did not opt for coffee or food, rather I opted for their iced matcha latte. I know.. this spot is known for their "joe" but they're just as popular for their "juice" hence the name!! & Various other bevvies. Felt the need to cool down so an iced matcha latte did the trick. It was creamy, lightly sweetened and refreshing. Just the right hue of bright green within the cup and I sipped away while on my excursion. The service was just OK though and they seemed super busy. Yeah I know it's the airport but they really weren't fixating on the details. I initially ordered a medium beverage, but they gave me a small one instead. This caught my eye immediately and I told them to remake my drink. They did without any hesitation. I was glad to have my medium sized iced drink as I was sharing it with my favorite person. Mm crisp matcha moments! Something different than Starbucks, thank goodness. This might be their only location in MN? Not sure. It was busy. I'll revisit in the near future. Just glad this airport has a few options besides SB - what a refreshing change. To the workers that work at this location, please focus on details and keep this place clean and non-disheveled. Bbyes.

name: International Wolf Center
description: A zoos business in Ely reviewed based on Sara's firsthand visit.
review: Such a cool little spot to view wolves in their natural habitat! Service was great and informative upon entering the wolf center. Staff was helpful in regards to the history of the wolves within the area and the pack of wolves that currently live at the center. It was a display they held and staff showed a few artifacts that were quite helpful in understanding wolves and their current living arrangements. Everyone got to view the current wolves behind a glass wall and saw them in their natural wild sanctuary. It was pretty neat seeing how they interact in their daily life and how they are common to spot in the city of Ely. They even have a museum section with further information and artifacts to learn from, as well as a small cinema to view a video. The video pertains to the lifestyle and the habits of the wolves and gives a general brief history of the wolves being introduced to the area. I love how interactive this spot was, they had plenty of things to see and do. They also have a small gift shop to purchase items from. I can definitely see myself visiting this spot if in the area. Just seeing all the wolves within the city of Ely was neat. It's a great place to visit when venturing through the area up north MN. International Wolf Center is a must if bringing friends or family up north. Into the wild you go!

name: Cedar Coffee Company
description: A coffee & tea spot in Two Harbors remembered for latte and an overall positive visit.
review: This place was awesome! All huddled and cuddled within a quiet corner of two harbors. I love that city and it was pretty neat finding this coffee shoppe on a whim whilst traveling through the north shores. Coffee was great as well as their matcha latte. I've been digging warm matcha latte and asked for it to be sweetened with cardamom syrup. Absolutely phenomenon. Cardamom pairs sooo well with matcha - what a matcha made in sight! No pun intended. Everything is practically made in house here, including their house made syrups, baked goods and savory food items. I loved their in house made scone.. warm, buttery and tender. They had a few scone selections to choose from, but we went for the blueberry coconut scone. Tasty and paired well with our beverages. We were also hungry and grabbed their chicken sandwich as well as their Thai style wrap. The wrap consisted of curried veggies, spicy Thai style peanut sauce wrapped up in a toasted lavash wrap bread. Yum. The roasted veggies had an Indian style flavor and paired well with the peanut sauce tucked in, very fusion style wrap. It was nice to eat a flavorful vegetarian lunch item that day, whilst traveling through the city. Indoors seating was plentiful but it was nice to sit outside in their backyard, immersed within a grove of many trees. Weather was refreshing in regards to MN style summers and a perfect little spot to visit before venturing out to a hike. I recommend Cedar Coffee if in the two harbors area. It's lively and adds a splash of coffee color before journeying towards your next adventure. Until next time!

name: Jang Guem Tofu & BBQ
description: A korean spot in Sugar Land remembered for the usual tofu soups and an overall positive visit.
review: Decent food, terrible service. I've been dining here for years and the menu has gone through a few changes. I used to love their kimchi dumplings that were made purely made out of kimchi and nothing else. They used to be crisp, warm and delightful. Back when the restaurant used to give a damn. I asked if I could order that and noticed it's no longer on the menu. They mentioned that it's always mixed with pork. Negative! Sure, maybe your new updated menu, but take a look at your menu from 3 years ago. The waiter spoke with a cold and condescending attitude. I thought to myself, why argue with someone that has barely worked here for that long? Ordered the vegetarian dumplings instead. Mediocre. Moving on. I ordered the usual tofu soups that I like getting from here. Sure their soups are good, but definitely on the salty side. With a condescending attitude, I bet I can't make an adjustment to any soup that I'm willing to order. Their banchan is just okay. Want a refill of your banchan? Good luck flagging down the waiter. Music is blaring loud and awfully obnoxious within a small dine in restaurant. Again, some of the food items are good here. Decent portions and their beef bulgogi is decent as well. Piping warm and fresh.. crackling on stone iron sets.. but damn... Nevermind the salt! Mind blown.

name: PJ's Coffee
description: A coffee & tea spot in Pearland remembered for coffee and an overall positive visit.
review: I like this little spot! I really do. My biggest gripe is the air ventilation and all the house flies swarming around the cafe. It literally smells like old oil in here and the ventilation is not the best. But let's get to the good stuff.. shall we? PJs offers some unique coffee drinks and treats. There are far too few locations within the greater Houston area so it's nice to visit this particular location from time to time. I've visited another location in the past which was in another state. They've got some great iced drinks here such as their lattes, mocha and seasonal drinks. The seasonal king cake is good here as well as their beignets. The beignets are fresh & made to order. They are decent.. nothing home to write about. The case near the register is stocked up on cookies, muffins and scones etc. Seating is decent as well. They've got a few chairs and sofas to lounge upon.. not the biggest spot though. The drive thru will get ya in and out in a jiffy.. good for when you're in a rush. This spot is far from me so I doubt I'll be visiting anytime soon.. hoping they can open up more locations. Other than that it's a warm spot with some aromatic coffee.

name: Turkish Cultural Center
description: A cultural center business in Fondren Southwest reviewed based on Sara's firsthand visit.
review: The Turkish Cultural Center is such a warm and welcoming spot. They often host all kinds of events here, such as community or multi-cultural events. I have been visiting the "Turquoise/ Raindrop Center" for over a decade plus. This is a fun gathering spot for all, no matter what age bracket you fall under. The building itself is quite unique and the marble for it was imported from Turkey. They have a small café inside the cultural center, as well as a prayer room. The folks that run this place, such as the staff, are all incredibly warm and friendly. This is a wonderful spot to visit, it will surely make you feel like you're out of country, or completely elsewhere. It gives me the travel bug to visit Turkiye, but it also gives me an appreciation of living in such a diverse city such as Houston. Check-out this cultural center; it is warm and welcoming to all, no matter your origin or background. You can even subscribe to their email list in order to ensure that you don't miss out on any events! A cool home away from home spot, they even have a park in the backyard for children. See it for yourself!

name: Golem's Gate - Gaming and Geekdom
description: A tabletop games business in Chinatown reviewed based on Sara's firsthand visit.
review: This is such a neat little mom and pop game store that is tucked in a quiet and cozy little part of town. The store owners, Tama and Jason are friendly, they will be quick to show you around & answer any questions you may have. They have a variety of books, miniatures, plushies and board games. Many gaming accessories for those that are into that type of stuff. Very fantasy like spot that will buzz the imagination of any that walks into the shoppe. You can also rent a board game and play with friends. Oh Tuesday evenings, the community hosts dungeons and dragons board game nights. A popular game from the 80s that has definitely had a revamp and has its own return into the world of board games. This is a fun little store where you can really be yourself and tap into your imagination. Dressing up in costumes is allowed and you can play the role of any character that comes to mind. Halloween is probably such a fun little time to explore Golems Gate, as well as any other seasonal holiday. Bring in your friends to this store and have fun! The more the merrier. This spot is a little nostalgic for those that love anything retro as well. A place where you can chat it up, put your phones away and do something a bit different. How's that for nostalgia? Cheers!

name: Zoa Moroccan Kitchen - Bellaire
description: A moroccan spot in Bellaire remembered for tea and an overall positive visit.
review: This was the third Zoa Moroccan Kitchen location that I have visited within Houston. They have locations all around the city and are rather convenient for visiting over lunch or dinner. So far with this location? Unimpressed and left much to be desired. This location is super skimpy with their portions and the price point is heavy. For two bowls, 1 bread and 1 green tea, you'll shell out about $30 and leave feeling a bit underwhelmed. Not sure why they are so skimpy with their portions and their service. Food was good, warm and flavorful, but I've had better at their other locations. This location is quite small and grab and go style as well. Parking is a bit small and limited and as mentioned, this location is smaller than the other ones that I have visited. With the food: The meats were tender and their toppings were decent. Unfortunately, I may never revisit ever again due to their lack of decent portions of their bowls and the overall presentation of their meals. I'm already hungry after writing this review and I was just visiting with their location not that long ago - LOL. Their super sweet Moroccan green tea is great, but honestly, I can make that at home (Atay Bi Nana). We don't have that many Moroccan food choices in Houston, I wish Zoa could do a bit better. Probably wont revisit this location ever again as mentioned. Until next time!

name: HQ BRGRS
description: A burgers spot in Majorstuen remembered for bread and an overall positive visit.
review: Juicy, delish and fresh burgers. Ordered a regular cheeseburger and was quite delighted with my meal. I normally don't eat burgers - but the one I ate last night definitely satisfied my craving. The beef patty was large, juicy and savory. The bread buns were soft and fresh. We also ordered french fries that came with aioli. The french fries were thick, like pomme frites and served with tiny little forks. Just delish, crisp, and tasted great with the aioli. I ate one too many fries and devoured most of my burger. Had to attend a concert that night, and this meal kept me full and satisfied. Glad we didn't end up eating at Olivia's next door (fancy Italian restaurant). We were in a rush, and our burgers were cooked up in a timely manner. The prices are pretty good for what you get, as the quantity is sufficient enough. All in all, I recommend HQ BRGRS. Will definitely visit again and try something else off the menu.

name: Christina's Donuts
description: A donuts business in Glendale reviewed after a visit that included cake.
review: Randomly spotted this place from across the street. It was glowing and taunting me to come inside. I was actually pretty hungry and realized that I hadn't eaten in awhile - so I decided to stop in and grab a few donuts with my sister. It was night time and I seriously thought they would have ran out of most of their selection. But that wasn't the case. So I picked up the apple fritter, cake donut and crueller. All three are my favorite and I was happy to eat a bite of each - yummy! The donuts were fresh, crisp and not too large. They are dirt cheap so the small sizes did not bother me. I liked how the donuts weren't too sweet. They satisfied my craving and kept me a bit full until dinner. These are just standard donuts - nothing fancy. We didn't experience any rude service - I think the man behind the counter was working as fast as he could. Donuts were around $3.30 in total.. again.. super cheap and simple. I'll definitely be back if in the area. They seem to serve up sandwiches are cold drinks as well. But i'll probably just stick to the donuts.

Good job Nissan, please continue to provide some great service with your loyal customers. By the way, the interior lobby looks completely different. They have renovated the space to provide better comfort for customers while they wait for their car.

I ordered a brownie and cafe latte on a Friday night. My latte was very sweet, flat and cold. It didn't even come with a saucer, so I had to carefully hold my coffee mug. Desserts didn't look that appealing, so I ordered a simple chocolate studded brownie. My brownie never showed up. I got up and had to ask for it, in which case they had forgotten about it. Brownie was way too sweet. They were definitely short staffed, and the cafe was unclean and unkempt. Black Walnut SL doesn't have the appeal and charm that it used to have.

name: Alpha Dessert Juice Cafe - Hillcroft
description: A desserts spot in Gulfton remembered for the cold coffee drink and an overall positive visit.
review: The cafe has expanded and it looks completely different inside, at least last time I visited. Which is rarely never. Their are murals and photographs of the Pakistani culture and history. I think that's great and should be represented in a cafe such as Agha Juice. You can't go wrong with their "kulfi" which is basically Pakistani ice-cream that is thick and creamy. The flavor is super sweet because of the condensed milk. But the texture and flavor is great. You can get it as a stick or as a chopped up plate of kulfi. They have snacks and foods as well, which I'm not too familiar with, honestly. A bit too heavy for my liking anyway. But maybe the burgers are good? I came here on a hot and sweltering day, longing for something with coffee. Should have know that I cant get decent coffee inside of a south Asian cafe. I ordered the cold coffee drink - which was essentially an ice cream shake consisting of coffee ice cream, milk and ice. Not of my liking and it was too heavy and light tasting. But if creamy milk shakes are your thing, then you might dig it. The guy at the front took forever to make my drink and I had to remind him of my order. The service was off and the employee's need better training. Other than that, I suppose its better to stick to their kulfi, falooda, and south Asian inspired drinks and desserts.

description: A tex-mex spot in Galleria/Uptown remembered for burrito and an overall positive visit.
review: Good Baja - California style cuisine, that serves up burritos, enchiladas, and much more. I have tried the fish tacos, cheese and spinach enchiladas. The enchiladas were hot, cheesy, and generously filled. Overall the food here is good, and they serve up a few items during lunch that I want to try, such as the fish burrito. Once you've ordered, you get to grab a basket and pile up corn tortillas, and choose salsa's at the salsa bar. The concept reminds me of the California style cantina's that I miss. Its good to have Berryhill here in Texas. I also enjoy the fact that they play classic dance music here at night. :)

name: Tacos A Go Go Midtown
description: A tex-mex spot in Midtown remembered for taco and an overall positive visit.
review: Tacos A Go-Go serves up some good tacos. Their isn't anything amazing about the tacos.. they are just okay. The taco shack is definitely a great place to chill with friends. Right when you enter you`ll notice a burst of colours the interior has to offer. One wall has a solid blue wall painted with different symbols and pictures. I like the feel of the place. I also love the outside of this place, and how the entrance of the lady wearing a big hat outside just draws you in. I have tried both the vegetarian and the seafood (fish) taco. They were both good. A bit on the small side though. The fish was fresh, and perfectly grilled. Juicy and moist, the fish complimented well with the coarseness of the corn tortilla. The SALSA here is all that I will ever truly come back for! It is a beautiful peachy colour. The taste is unique, and unlike the typical tomato based salsas. Its super hot but addicting served with a side of crispy tortilla chips. I like the area this place is situated in. There is a lovely walk you can enjoy afterward. There is also the Metro Rail which you can catch.

The breads are baked daily, and are lightly sweetened. They have various and unique flavors to select from. I have had their croissant, coconut bread, and pound cakes. They were all equally buttery and tasty. The prices are reasonable, and the desserts are a nice size. I will definitely come back soon to pick up some treats and serve them to my guests. I love the fact that these baked goodies are light and flavorful.

description: A coffee & tea business in Montrose reviewed after a visit that included tea.
review: Te House of Tea has a lovely selection of tea's from around the world I am an avid tea drinker who drinks various types of teas, so I was pleased with the selection offered at Te House. My friend and I both shared the 'metropolis' tea which was quite fragrant and light. The amount of tea in the kettle was enough for the both of us to share. I also had this vegetarian soup which consisted of sweet potatoes and kale. It was sweet, spicy, and heartwarming. I like their menu selection and how many of the items are vegetarian and vegan friendly. Te House of Tea has live music on the weekend, as well as small performances. I like the atmosphere of this place, it is quaint and cozy. Its a good place to catch up with a friend, enjoy a light meal and douse it down with a comforting cup of tea.

name: Ruggles Café Bakery
description: A american spot in West University remembered for the dill potato salad and an overall positive visit.
review: Great food and good customer service. Came in with a group of six friends on a random and cold Wednesday night. To our luck, they had a dinner entree + dessert deal for Wednesday. We all ordered our entrees consisting of sandwiches, burgers and pasta. Everyone seemed to enjoy their meal. The Mediterranean salmon pasta that my sister ordered was flavorful and delicious. I had ordered the black bean burger which was quite filling and tasty as well. I loved the crunchy bread my sandwich came with. The entree came with a choice of a side, so I opted for the dill potato salad. The potatoes were comforting and savory. The desserts were great as well. I opted for the domino cake which was quite rich and full of good chocolate. My sweet tooth was definitely satisfied with this cake. I had always wanted to check out Ruggles Cafe Bakery. It was a nice change from Ruggles Green, which I frequent often in Sugar Land. Both restaurants are similar, but Ruggles Cafe has several more options for dessert. The menu was a nice change as well, ranging with many food options. Will definitely come back in the future when i'm the mood for some good comfort food in the area.

name: Mitchell's Ice Cream
description: A ice cream & frozen yogurt spot in Bernal Heights remembered for to grab a ticket and wait for my number to be called and an overall positive visit.
review: THE ICE-CREAM AT MITCHELL'S IS SO GOOD I FORGOT TO TAKE A PICTURE! Yep... it was that good. I came in on a random weekday night.. around 9 pm. The brick and mortar was packed with folks coming in left and right. This is probably the first ice cream shop in which I had to grab a ticket and wait for my number to be called. I felt a bit helpless in deciding on which flavors to settle upon. I was totally in the mood for a warm and decadent brownie fudge sundae. But to my dismay, they didn't have that on the menu. I also didn't want to continuously sample every flavour in the bin. So I made the brave decision and settled upon the toasted almond ice cream and the espresso toffee ice cream. I felt a bit rebellious in choosing a caffeinated flavored ice cream at night - but it was totally worth it. Being a chocoholic, I asked for hot fudge to be smothered on my ice cream. I was given two large scoops of ice cream that was swimming in hot fudge sauce. Oh my gosh, totally worth every bite! Mitchell's ice cream is super fluffy, creamy, and fresh. I ate every bite possible in my cup. So glad to have ventured down here in the Mission and try Mitchell's. The best ice cream spot in San Francisco! You'll be hooked like a sugar hooker. Give it a try!

review: Good solid coffee that reminds me of the amazing spots in Houston (Home). Latte's are super creamy yet light at the same time. The flavor of the beans are fully roasted yet display a smooth taste. My friend got the hot chocolate which looked just as good. The sweets were nice as well, such as the brownie. Its quite small inside, yet its a nice little spot to drop by with friends.

name: Mai Colachi - Sugar Land
description: A halal spot in Sugar Land remembered for bread and an overall positive visit.
review: Authentic and flavorful Pakistani cuisine served in an elegant manner. The ambiance and environment complement the theme as well. My family and I enjoyed our dinner here at Mai Colachi. I am quite picky with Pakistani cuisine and I normally do not eat it at restaurants.. Because food at such restaurants tend to create heavy dishes full of oil with just one note of flavor. But the cuisine here was nice, presentable, and tasty. Every dish had its own unique appeal to it. The bread served was fluffy and soft and the passion fruit drink and ice-cream dessert were nice as well. Will definitely be back again with my family. The restaurant is located in a nice and convenient little plaza in Sugar Land. Will be sure to drop by one day when i'm in the mood for spicy and unique food.
